inputs_used: head/tail + key-cardinality scan of data/train.csv, data/test.csv, data/sample_submission.csv
forbidden_inputs_avoided: prior local run artifacts (STATUS.md, experiments*.json) were NOT read — dossier is a fresh prior
task_family: time-series forecast (daily panel regression; 75 country x store x product series)

data_shape.panel_completeness: complete and balanced: 75 x 1826 = 136950 train rows, 75 x 365 = 27375 test rows; no missing cells

product: Using LLMs to Improve Your Coding
Using LLMs to Train More LLMs
Using LLMs to Win Friends and Influence People
Using LLMs to Win More Kaggle Competitions

data_shape.key_overlap: train and test share identical country/store/product level sets — no unseen categories

target.name: num_sold
target.note: strictly positive integer counts; no zero rows, so SMAPE's near-zero blowup is not triggered by the target itself

data_shape.id: monotone integer, disjoint between train (0..136949) and test (136950..164324); id encodes the same ordering as (date, country, store, product)

test_window.evidence: test dates span 2022-01-01..2022-12-31, strictly after the train span 2017-01-01..2021-12-31; zero date overlap; id ranges disjoint and contiguous after train; every (country, store, product) combination in test also appears in train, so the split is a pure forward time cut, not a group holdout

split_policy.scheme: time-based holdout / expanding-window CV on whole years: fold k trains on years < y_k and validates on year y_k (e.g. validate 2019, 2020, 2021); equivalently TimeSeriesSplit over sorted dates with whole-year folds. Final model refits on 2017-2021 to predict 2022.
split_policy.forbidden: shuffled KFold and any row-level random split — leaks same-day/adjacent-day information across the 75 parallel series and produces measured ~4.5x optimism on this exact competition (4.56 shuffled vs 20.41 time-split SMAPE, per TASK-TS-FUTURE)
extra_cautions: GroupKFold on series id is also wrong here: test contains the SAME series, only later in time — the generalization axis is time, not group
2020 contains a COVID-shaped regime break; a single 2021-only validation year may be optimistic/pessimistic relative to 2022 — report per-year fold scores, not just the mean
any lag/rolling feature must be computed within-series and shifted so that no value from date >= the validation fold's start leaks backward

metric.name: SMAPE
traps: asymmetric: under-prediction is penalized harder than over-prediction of the same absolute size, so the SMAPE-optimal point forecast sits below the conditional mean — fitting plain L2 on the raw target is misaligned

scale-free / relative: small-volume series (e.g. Kaggle Learn in low-volume countries) contribute as much per row as high-volume ones, so per-series normalization matters and a global RMSE-driven model will over-serve the large series
target is strictly positive (min 2), so the classic SMAPE-at-zero singularity does not bite, but predictions must still be clamped to a positive floor

L1-in-log space is a good tractable surrogate: minimizing MAE on log(num_sold) approximates relative error; do the SMAPE computation itself (including any rounding/clamping post-processing) inside the metric function so every CV and blend candidate is scored on the real objective
integer target: test whether rounding predictions to integers helps or hurts under SMAPE — decide on CV, inside the metric

external_data.rules_status: RESOLVED: external data permitted per official rules 7.C (verified 2026-07-29); config.yaml corrected.
external_data.reasoning: The country dimension carries level information that no in-file covariate explains: five countries with very different economies (Argentina, Canada, Estonia, Japan, Spain) share identical store/product/date structure, so cross-country differences in num_sold are a pure country-level multiplier. Task prior TASK-TS-FUTURE records that accepted solutions on this exact task family join per-country GDP, and that the analogous tps-jan-2022 join moved CV SMAPE 6.1551 -> 4.1793. The train window additionally straddles 2020-2021 (COVID), while the test year 2022 does not — a regime the official files cannot describe.

candidates.indicator: GDP per capita (and GDP level / growth as alternates)
candidates.leakage_rule: only values dated <= the prediction year; lag=0 (same-year value allowed, the historical-solution convention). 2022 values may be unpublished at snapshot time — carry-forward the last available year and log the snapshot date
deterministic future — no leakage; safe to generate for 2022

candidates.indicator: country codes / geo groupings (for hemisphere, i.e. seasonality sign: Argentina is southern hemisphere, the other four northern)

candidates.leakage_rule: only values dated <= the row date, lag=0; relevant to the 2020-2021 portion of train. NOT usable as a test-time feature (2022 values would have to be forecast) — use it only to model/deweight the 2020-2021 anomaly, never as a predictor for 2022. ~178 MB one-time cache, download must be explicitly allowed

external_data.whitelist_check: all four candidates are drawn from the External-data whitelist table in knowledge/task_priors.md; the two whitelisted sources not proposed are Exchange rates (ECB SDMX) — no currency column in the data — which was considered and rejected, leaving no off-whitelist candidate in this dossier
external_data.in_data_fallback_if_blocked: the country multiplier is estimable from the official data alone: per-country share of total num_sold is near-constant across years and can be used directly as a learned ratio, which is what the GDP join is a smooth proxy for. This fallback needs no external fetch and is legal under external_data_allowed: false.

data_level: join World Bank GDP per capita by country x year (lag=0, carry-forward for 2022) as a country-level scale covariate — gated on the external-data rule check
join national holiday flags by country x date (plus day-before / day-after and a year-end / new-year window flag) — deterministic, safe for 2022
hemisphere flag from ISO region table so seasonal harmonics can flip sign for Argentina

ratio decomposition without external data: model total daily volume, then multiply by per-country / per-store / per-product share ratios estimated from train (the classic multiplicative panel decomposition this data's balanced structure invites)
Fourier / calendar features from the date alone: day-of-week, week-of-year sin/cos harmonics, month, day-of-year, is-month-start/end, and a year index for trend
explicit COVID-regime handling for 2020-2021: an indicator or per-country sample weight so the anomaly does not distort the 2022 forecast; optionally quantified with OWID COVID (train-side only)

within-series lag / rolling-mean features are available only for the first test horizon unless recursively forecast — prefer calendar+ratio features over lags for a 365-day-ahead horizon, or use a per-series seasonal-naive baseline (same day-of-year last year) as an explicit feature
model_level: L1 objective (MAE) rather than L2 for this SMAPE metric, per TASK-MAE-METRIC
train on log1p(num_sold) with L1 loss and invert with expm1 — approximates the relative-error geometry SMAPE scores
put clamping to a positive floor and any integer rounding INSIDE the metric function so every CV fold and every blend candidate is scored on the post-processed prediction
native categorical handling in the GBDT for country/store/product (all features are categorical + date-derived) rather than one-hot, per TASK-CAT-ONLY

strong non-GBDT baseline is likely competitive here: pure multiplicative decomposition / seasonal-naive-with-ratios, because the panel is complete, balanced and synthetic-looking — include one as a blend member for decorrelation

add one shallow, heavily regularized, diverse-library member to the blend before optimizing weights (TASK-BLEND-DECOR); for the blend weights prefer a closed-form/convex solve over random Dirichlet search
evaluate blends on the same forward-in-time folds — blend weights fit on a shuffled split inherit the same 4.5x optimism as the base models

task_prior_match_notes.TASK-TS-FUTURE: date column present and test period (2022) strictly after train (2017-2021); triggers the mandatory time-based split and the macro-external-data assessment
task_prior_match_notes.TASK-TS-CALENDAR: daily-resolution series keyed by country x store x product — exactly the trigger; calendar + holiday features indicated
task_prior_match_notes.TASK-MAE-METRIC: metric is SMAPE, an MAE-family relative metric; L1 objective and post-processing-inside-the-metric apply
task_prior_match_notes.TASK-CAT-ONLY: partial match — every non-date feature (country, store, product) is categorical, all low-cardinality; encoding is less decisive than in the full trigger case (no high-cardinality column), so treat native-categorical GBDT handling as a baseline rather than 'the whole game'
task_prior_match_notes.TASK-BLEND-DECOR: forward-looking: applies at the blend stage once a member pool exists; recorded now so the shallow-regularized decorrelator is not forgotten
